kept.claim: runSplitQuery now calls applyTemplateVariables (which adds ad-hoc filters) on targets that DataSourceWithBackend.query will interpolate again (and the shard path adds a third pass), so ad-hoc filters that land as label filters after a parser are appended repeatedly.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Ad-hoc filters are now applied twice (three times under sharding) and pile up as duplicate label filters

**Severity:** MEDIUM — every split Loki query that has a parser gets the same ad-hoc label filter appended once per interpolation pass, so the query sent to Loki differs from what the user built and grows with each pass.

### The Problem

```ts
const queries = request.targets
  .filter((query) => !query.hide)
  .filter((query) => query.expr)
  .map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters));
```

`LokiDatasource.applyTemplateVariables` (`datasource.ts:1110`) is not idempotent. It runs `templateSrv.replace` **and** `addAdHocFilters(expr, adhocFilters)`. The split sub-requests are later run through `datasource.runQuery` -> `super.query` -> `DataSourceWithBackend.query`, which calls `this.applyTemplateVariables(q, request.scopedVars, request.filters)` again on every target (`packages/grafana-runtime/src/utils/DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185`). `request.filters` is still set on each sub-request, because `querySplitting.ts` builds sub-requests by spreading `request`.

- Plain `lokiQuerySplitting` path: the filter was applied once before this PR and is applied twice now.
- `lokiShardSplitting` path: `runShardSplitQuery` applies it (`shardQuerySplitting.ts:52`), then passes each group into `runSplitQuery` (`shardQuerySplitting.ts:163`), which applies it again, and then `DataSourceWithBackend.query` applies it a third time. The updated test encodes this: `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)` for a single target.

### Theory / Proof

`addAdHocFilters` calls `addLabelToQuery` (`modifyQuery.ts:147`) for each filter. The stream-selector branch deduplicates (`addFilterToStreamSelector` checks `labelExists`, `modifyQuery.ts:494`). The label-filter branch does not. When the query has a parser and every stream selector already has a matcher (`modifyQuery.ts:200-211`), for example `sum(count_over_time({app="x"} | logfmt [$__auto]))`, the filter goes through `addFilterAsLabelFilter` (`modifyQuery.ts:511`). That function always appends `` | key=`value` `` with no existence check. Each pass sees the result of the previous one and appends again:

```
{app="x"} | logfmt | level=`error` | level=`error`                  // split path
{app="x"} | logfmt | level=`error` | level=`error` | level=`error`   // shard path
```

### What happens today vs. what will break

Repeating an `=`/`!=`/`=~` filter gives the same result set, so the numbers usually look right. But:
- Query inspector and query history show a different, longer query than the one the user wrote.
- Loki evaluates the redundant stages for every log line in every chunk and shard.
- The template pass also runs more than once (see the separate comment on re-interpolation).

### Research

Other Grafana datasources that pre-interpolate before calling `super.query` override `applyTemplateVariables` to be idempotent, or they pass a request that no longer carries `filters`/`scopedVars`. The base `DataSourceWithBackend.query` contract assumes targets are raw and interpolates them exactly once.

### Recommendation

Interpolate once, then clear the ad-hoc filters on the request that is passed down, so later passes are no-ops for filters:

```ts
const queries = request.targets
  .filter((query) => !query.hide)
  .filter((query) => query.expr)
  .map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters));
// sub-requests must not re-apply ad-hoc filters
request = { ...request, filters: [] };
```

Alternatively, make `runSplitQuery` interpolate only when it is called from `datasource.query` (not from the shard path), and make `addFilterAsLabelFilter` skip filters that already exist. Add a test with `request.filters` set and a parser query that asserts the final `expr` contains the filter exactly once.
kept.evidence: querySplitting.ts:299 now calls applyTemplateVariables, which runs addAdHocFilters each time (datasource.ts:1110-1136). Sub-requests keep request.filters (querySplitting.ts:174-180), and DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185 re-applies them. The shard path adds a third pass (shardQuerySplitting.ts:52, then :163 into runSplitQuery). addFilterToStreamSelector deduplicates (modifyQuery.ts:494), but addFilterAsLabelFilter (modifyQuery.ts:511-540) does not, so queries with a parser get duplicated ` | key=`v`` stages. Before this PR, neither path applied ad-hoc filters before the backend pass (the shard path's interpolateVariablesInQueries was called without filters). No test covers ad-hoc filters. Result sets are unchanged because the duplicate filters are ANDed together; the impact is query bloat and a sent query that differs from what the user wrote.

kept.claim: templateSrv.replace now runs on already-interpolated expressions (split path twice, shard path three times), so a single-value variable whose value contains `$other` gets re-expanded.
kept.body:
## [ISSUE] Template variables are now interpolated repeatedly, so `$` text inside a variable value gets re-expanded

**Severity:** LOW — textbox/constant variable values that contain `$name` text are substituted a second time before the query reaches Loki.

### The Problem

`runSplitQuery` now runs `templateSrv.replace` on `expr`, `step` and `legendFormat` (through `applyTemplateVariables`). `DataSourceWithBackend.query` (`packages/grafana-runtime/src/utils/DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185`) then runs the same replacement on the already interpolated output. Under shard splitting it runs three times.

### Theory / Proof

For non-multi, non-include-all variables, `interpolateQueryExpr` (`datasource.ts:787-791`) returns the value unescaped. Take a textbox variable `search` with value `cost$region` and a dashboard that also has a variable `region=eu`. The query `{app="x"} |= "$search"` becomes `|= "cost$region"` on the first pass and `|= "costeu"` on the second. Before this PR the non-sharded split path interpolated exactly once, so the user's literal value was sent unchanged.

### What happens today vs. what will break

Most values contain no `$`, so nothing changes for them. Line filters and regexes that search for literal `$`-prefixed tokens (shell variables, currency, template strings in logs) silently match the wrong text whenever the name after `$` is also a dashboard variable.

### Research

`TemplateSrv.replace` has no marker for "already interpolated" output. Interpolation is only safe when it runs exactly once, which is why `DataSourceWithBackend` does it at a single point.

### Recommendation

Interpolate at a single point. Either keep the pre-interpolated targets and make the backend call skip interpolation for them, or interpolate only the fields that the splitting logic needs (for example `step` for `calculateStep`) on a copy used for planning, and send the original targets to `runQuery`:

```ts
const planningQueries = queries.map((q) => ({ ...q, step: datasource.interpolateString(q.step ?? '', request.scopedVars) }));
```
kept.evidence: The split path now runs 2 templateSrv passes (querySplitting.ts:299 and DataSourceWithBackend.ts:185) where the base ran 1; the shard path runs 3 (it ran 2 before the PR). interpolateQueryExpr (datasource.ts:787-791) returns non-multi values unescaped, so a `$other` inside a value survives the first pass and is expanded on the next. step and legendFormat are replaced with no format function, so they are exposed too. Nothing guards against this, and the tests mock replace and check only a single pass.
